sections.heading: Glossary term: Degree
sections.body: In mathematics a degree (symbol °) is a measure of angle. One degree is 1/360th of a full circle. It can be expressed as a decimal number or it can be divided into arcminutes (symbol ′) where 60′ is 1°, and arcseconds (symbol ″) where 60″ is 1′. One arcsecond is 1/3600th of a degree, an extremely small angle. Degrees measure the apparent size of an object (see angular diameter) and its position on the celestial sphere. See also: declination, right ascension, altitude, and azimuth. On Earth: latitude and longitude. They are also used to measure angular distance between objects on the celestial sphere. The width of your fist at arm’s length is about 10°; from the horizon to the zenith is 90°. Depending on the scale, a telescope’s resolution and field-of-view can be expressed in degrees, arcminutes, or arcseconds. Alternate meaning: A unit in the measure of temperature, used with the Fahrenheit or Celsius scales. The Celsius scale is defined by the freezing point of water at sea level being 0°C and the boiling point of water being 100°C.  A change of one degree Celsius is the same as a change of one kelvin but they have different zero points. The zero point of the kelvin scale is absolute zero, the lowest temperature, -273.15°C.  In the older Fahrenheit system a change of one degree is the same as a change of 5/9ths of a degree Celsius or kelvin.

Glossary term: Degree

Description: In mathematics a degree (symbol °) is a measure of angle. One degree is 1/360th of a full circle. It can be expressed as a decimal number or it can be divided into arcminutes (symbol ′) where 60′ is 1°, and arcseconds (symbol ″) where 60″ is 1′. One arcsecond is 1/3600th of a degree, an extremely small angle.

Degrees measure the apparent size of an object (see angular diameter) and its position on the celestial sphere. See also: declination, right ascension, altitude, and azimuth. On Earth: latitude and longitude. They are also used to measure angular distance between objects on the celestial sphere. The width of your fist at arm’s length is about 10°; from the horizon to the zenith is 90°. Depending on the scale, a telescope’s resolution and field-of-view can be expressed in degrees, arcminutes, or arcseconds.

Alternate meaning: A unit in the measure of temperature, used with the Fahrenheit or Celsius scales. The Celsius scale is defined by the freezing point of water at sea level being 0°C and the boiling point of water being 100°C. A change of one degree Celsius is the same as a change of one kelvin but they have different zero points. The zero point of the kelvin scale is absolute zero, the lowest temperature, -273.15°C. In the older Fahrenheit system a change of one degree is the same as a change of 5/9ths of a degree Celsius or kelvin.

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. sections.body_ru: В математике градус (символ °) — это мера угла. Один градус составляет 1/360 полного круга. Его можно выразить десятичным числом или разделить на угловые минуты (символ ′), где 60′ составляет 1°, и угловые секунды (символ ″), где 60″ составляет 1′. Одна угловая секунда — это 1/3600 градуса, чрезвычайно малый угол. Градусы измеряют видимый размер объекта (см. угловой диаметр) и его положение на небесной сфере. См. также: склонение, прямое восхождение, высота и азимут. На Земле: широта и долгота. Они также используются для измерения углового расстояния между объектами на небесной сфере. Ширина вашего кулака на расстоянии вытянутой руки составляет около 10°; от горизонта до зенита — 90°. В зависимости от масштаба разрешение и поле зрения телескопа могут выражаться в градусах, угловых минутах или угловых секундах. Альтернативное значение: единица измерения температуры, используемая в шкалах Фаренгейта или Цельсия. Шкала Цельсия определяется точкой замерзания воды на уровне моря, равной 0°C, и точкой кипения воды, равной 100°C. Изменение на один градус Цельсия такое же, как изменение на один кельвин, но у них разные нулевые точки. Нулевая точка шкалы Кельвина — это абсолютный нуль, самая низкая температура, -273.15°C. В старой системе Фаренгейта изменение на один градус такое же, как изменение на 5/9 градуса Цельсия или кельвина.
